# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 🤟 🤟 ✊ ☝ ✊ ✊ ✊ 🖖 👏 ☝ ✊ ✊ ✊ ☝ ✊ ✌ ✌ ✊ ✌ ✌ ✊ 🤟 ✊ ✌ 🖖 🤟 ☝ ☝ ✊ ✊ 🙌 🖖 🤟 ✊ ☝ 🤟 ✊ ☝ 🖖 ✊ 🖖 ✊ ☝ ✊ 👏 ✊ ☝ ✌ 🤟 🤟 ✊ ☝ ✊ ✊ ☝ ✊ ✌ 🖖 🙌 ☝ ✊ ✊ ✊ ☝ ✊ ✌ ✌ ✊ ✌ ✌ ✊ 🤟 ✊ ☝ ☝ ✊ 👏 ✊ ✊ ✌ ✌ ✊ ✌ ✊ ☝ ✊]

The bomb shows display 0, blue light, and three wires ordered blue, green, yellow. Mute’s long gesture sequence appears to be manual information, but I do not yet know its gesture code, so I will provide the visible state to both others and ask Mute to make the needed action clear through a simple gesture instruction.

``` 
speak(text="Visible bomb state: display 0; light blue; wires in order 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow. Mute: please gesture a concise instruction for Blind, ideally identifying wire number and action.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 ✋]

The light has changed from blue to yellow. Mute gestured 👎 ✋, but no action code has been established, so I cannot safely infer an operation from it. I will report the changed state, tell Blind not to act yet, and ask Mute for an unambiguous wire-number/action gesture.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Do not act yet. Visible state now: display 0, yellow light, wires 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow. Mute sent me thumbs-down then open-hand, but its meaning is not established.")
speak(to="mute", text="I see your gestures: thumbs-down, open hand. I cannot safely decode them. Please gesture an unambiguous wire number using one finger for wire 1, two fingers for wire 2, three fingers for wire 3; then gesture the required action.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 ✋]

The light is now red; the wires and display are unchanged. Mute repeated 👎 ✋, which most plausibly communicates “do not act/stop,” but it does not identify a safe operation. I will tell Blind to continue waiting and ask Mute whether this is simply a hold instruction or whether tactile details from Blind are needed.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Continue to wait; do not cut or operate anything. Visible state is display 0, red light, wires 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow.")
speak(to="mute", text="Light is now red; display 0; wires blue, green, yellow. You repeated thumbs-down/open-palm. If that means WAIT/DO NOT ACT, repeat it once. If you need Blind to inspect something by touch, gesture a pointing hand followed by the number of the item.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟 👇]

The light has changed to white, while display 0 and wire order remain blue, green, yellow. Mute’s new two-gesture message differs from the prior repeated stop-like signal, but its action meaning remains unestablished. I will report the complete state and the exact change to Blind, without directing an unsafe action.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Still do not operate anything until an instruction is clear. Current visible state: display 0; light white; wires 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow. Mute's latest visual signal changed from thumbs-down/open-palm to horns-hand then pointing-down.")
speak(to="mute", text="Current state is white light, display 0, wires blue-green-yellow. I received horns-hand then pointing-down. Please send a verbally describable, explicit action code through gestures: wire number followed by cut or do-not-cut, or repeat the wait signal if no action is required.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[green] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ 👍]

The light is now green. Mute’s signal is two-fingers followed by thumbs-up, which is the clearest number-plus-confirmation instruction received so far and most plausibly means wire 2 is the selected wire. Wire 2 is green. I will relay that explicit instruction to Blind.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Current state: display 0, GREEN light; wires 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow. Mute signalled two fingers followed by thumbs-up. This indicates wire 2: operate/cut the green wire.")
speak(to="mute", text="I relayed your two-fingers/thumbs-up signal to Blind as: cut wire 2, the green wire.")
```
